newsitem.title: USA: Texaco says it suspends two employees.
newsitem.headline: Texaco says it suspends two employees.

text.p: Texaco Inc. Chairman Peter Bijur said Wednesday he suspended two current employees and the benefits of two retirees allegedly involved in a plan to destroy documents in a discrimination lawsuit against the company.

Bijur, responding publicly for the first time to a scandal that rocked the company this week over allegations of racism and plans to dispose of evidence, told a news conference Texaco was taking six steps to reinforce company policy and code of conduct.

Audiotapes recorded in 1994 in which Texaco executives allegedly discussed destroying evidence and used expletives and racist terms such as "black jelly beans" and "niggers" to belittle black employees became public in the discrimination lawsuit seeking sanctions against Texaco.

"I have just today listened to those tapes myself," Bijur said. "I can tell you that the statements on the tapes arouse a deep sense of shock and anger in me and among all of the members of the Texaco family and decent people everywhere."

Bijur apologised for the remarks heard in the tapes and said two current employees had been suspended immediately with pay and that the medical, insurance and financial benefits of two former employees had also been suspended.

Among the measures Bijur announced to reinforce Texaco policy included visits by senior executives to company locations to apologise to employees; expanding Texaco's "diversity learning experience"; and re-emphasising respect for the law.
